_comment: 🔮️ Coordination View 2.0's own contribution to the repository test platform: `ruststep` 0.4 registered as the independent ISO 10303-21 reader for this subset's `Ifc2x3Cv20Mutation` vocabulary, and the mutation catalog it is measured against. The vocabulary is NOT the ✳️any subset's -- ✳️any declares generic Part-21 graph editing (upsert-instance/remove-instance/set-header) and knows nothing about model view definitions, while every kind below is one rule of the CV2.0 conformance gate this repository already implements in production (`../🧬️schema/🦀️component.rs`'s `check_cv20_conformance`). The `semantic-ifc-v1` comparison profile is the ✳️any subset's own contribution, reused rather than copied: the exchange structure being compared is the same IFC2X3 Part-21 graph.

oracles.rationale: IFC2X3 is physically ISO 10303-21 (STEP physical file) syntax under the IFC2X3 EXPRESS schema, and `ruststep` 0.4 parses it exactly as it parses STEP AP214 -- already linked and already registered for the sibling `ifc 2x3/✳️any` and `step ap214/✳️any` subsets, and re-confirmed here against this subset's own real input (the committed 3464-entity slice of a real 21 MB IFC2X3 EDM export whose FILE_DESCRIPTION genuinely declares `ViewDefinition [CoordinationView_V2.0]`, parsed with zero errors). It has NO writer: `ast::ser::to_record` only builds an in-memory `Record` from an already-typed Rust struct, and no `Display`/`fmt::Formatter` impl exists on `Exchange`/`DataSection`/`Record`/`Parameter`. Per the fleet brief's §6 that rules out `@mode-differential` -- ruststep cannot be a second PRODUCER of mutated bytes -- so it is registered strictly as the INDEPENDENT READER: every mutation this subset's own dispatcher performs (via ruststep's real parse plus the standard-level from-scratch Part-21 writer at `../../../🧪️oracle/🦀️component.rs`, never this repository's own production `step::engine::part21` writer, which would compare the implementation against itself) is read back through a FRESH `ruststep::ast::Exchange::from_str` call before `semantic-ifc-v1` compares it. STRONGER REFERENCE EVALUATED AND NOT ADOPTED: `ifcopenshell` 0.8.4 (Python) is the canonical IFC toolkit, it both READS and WRITES IFC, and it would make a genuine `@mode-differential` possible for exactly these model-view-definition subsets; it was installed and imported successfully in this environment, and the repository's Python oracle host has landed (working precedent: `🗿️artifacts/📄️pdf/🧪️tests/extract-text-pdf-1-4/🐍️component.py` with `pypdf`). It was NOT adopted because putting a Python distribution on a generated host's import path requires an `oracleHostPackages` entry in the SHARED `✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🧪️oracle/🔣️component.json` -- `oracleHostPackagesFor` resolves host packages by owner prefix, and this subset's own manifest is not a prefix of the case owner `🗿️artifacts/🏗️ifc` -- and this wave's brief forbids an executor from editing the shared stdio manifest. That is a governance boundary, not a capability gap, and it is the single highest-value follow-up for all three IFC2X3 MVD subsets.
